demidik-kernel-definition: Section II, p.2, Eq. (3): the paper defines its quantum kernel as the squared overlap (fidelity) of the feature-map states
demidik-iqp-map-definition: Section III, p.2, Eq. (4): the paper writes the IQP feature map as a Hadamard layer then a diagonal unitary of RZ and RZZ rotations
demidik-longitudinal-iqp-definition: Section III, p.3, Eqs. (6) and (7) define the running-mean gate parameters per layer; Section V, p.4 restates the cumulative encoding
demidik-synthetic-setup: Section III, p.3: 100,000 samples, one feature in [0, 2pi], two time points, fidelity to a fixed reference with both values pi/2; the paper states it as its own setup
demidik-fl-setup: Section IV a), p.4: one to three biopsies per subject and the first 20 genes by Welch's t-test, stated as the paper's own preprocessing
demidik-ad-composition: Section IV b), p.4: 150 subjects, 64 demented, 72 non-demented, 14 transitioned; the counts add to 150
demidik-ad-task-no-mri: Section IV b), p.4: binary classification on CDR status from the listed features; MRI scan data left to future work
demidik-comparison-setup: Section IV, p.4: three feature maps, SVM trained by standard convex optimization, RBF given all time points as separate features
demidik-future-work-scale: Section V, p.4: the authors state that robustness and scalability on larger cohorts are not yet assessed, after noting the cohort-size difficulty
demidik-numerical-simulation-scope: Abstract, p.1: the evidence is stated to come from numerical simulations on synthetic and real-world datasets
demidik-datasets: Section IV a) and b), p.4: 32 subjects in two groups (nFL, tFL) and 150 subjects with 3 or 4 MRI scans, both stated as the paper's own datasets
demidik-limits: Section V, p.4: cohort-size difficulty and possible gain from tuning are stated as limits; the third clause is a concession ('Even if near-term quantum models remain classically simulable'), which the paper does state, so it is kept
deng-adjacency-encoding: Section on the graph correspondence, p.2, Eq. (3): the paper gives the explicit construction A = diag(c Delta, c Delta*) and says each GBS sample selects a submatrix; the detail of the rescaling factor c is in the Supplemental Material, which the text does not contain
deng-maxhaf-definition: p.2: the Max-Haf problem is defined in one sentence, quote verbatim and complete
deng-dense-subgraph-definition: p.2, Eq. (4): rendered page 2 shows density W(G_S) as the absolute value of the sum of the entries of the subgraph adjacency matrix, as the value says (the text layer drops the bars)
deng-nonideal-negative-terms: p.3, deviation (i): the paper states that the sampling matrix retrieved from its experiment is not always non-negative as in the original proposal; it names this as a departure it must consider
deng-experiment-setup: Introduction p.1 and Experiment section p.3: 50 single-mode squeezed states into a 144-mode network; a randomly generated, fully connected 144-mode interferometer
deng-algorithms-studied: p.3: RS and SA, and their GBS-enhanced variants, are the two stochastic algorithms studied
deng-maxhaf-fig2-setup: Figure 2 caption, p.3: mean photon click 21, 12-click samples post-selected, mean of 100 trials, shaded standard error
deng-density-fig2-setup: Figure 2 caption, p.3: 80-vertex subgraph in 144 vertices, mean click 61, 80-click samples, maximum over 120 trials for SA and mean over 20 for RS
deng-score-speed-definition-maxhaf: Figure 3 caption, p.4: both ratios are defined in the caption, with the 1000-step reference for the score advantage
deng-score-speed-definition-density: Figure 3 caption, p.4: score advantage at 10000 steps, and the speed-advantage target set at the RS value at 10000 steps
deng-hafnian-evaluation-machine: Scaling section, p.4 (page 5 of the item anchor): 'due to the computational overhead, we use the Sunway TaihuLight supercomputer to evaluate the Hafnian'
deng-fig4-setup: Figure 4 caption, p.5: target is the mean RS value at 10000 steps, 144-vertex full graph, photon click 10, mean photon number 7 (low noise) and 6 (high noise)
deng-gbs-setup-jiuzhang: Abstract, p.1: 144-mode fully connected photonic processor, photon clicks up to 80; the phrase 'quantum computational advantage regime' is the authors' own characterization, as the value says
deng-open-question-better-classical: Conclusion, p.6: the paper states it is open whether GBS beats improved classical and quantum-inspired algorithms, and that the enhancement can depend on the input graphs
derieux-framework-definition: Section 1.2, p.2, with Sections 2.1 to 2.3: the paper defines eQMARL as a split quantum critic with entangled inputs and joint measurement
derieux-joint-measurement: Section 2.3, p.4, Eq. (3): joint Pauli Z measurement over all qubits, value estimate V(o) = w(1 + <O>)/2 with learned scalar w
derieux-trusted-source: Section 2.1, p.4: the paper states the assumption of real-time entangled qubits from a trusted central source, and the pre-generation alternative
derieux-classical-channel-still-used: Section 2.5, p.5: rewards go to the server over a classical channel, and the classical channel also carries the critic-loss partial gradients
derieux-simulation-only: Section 3.2, p.6: tensorflow-quantum and cirq for quantum simulations; cluster with 128 CPU cores and 256 GB per node
derieux-baselines-definition: Section 3.2, p.6: the three baselines are listed with their critic locations and structure
derieux-training-schedules: Section 3.2, p.6: epochs, step limits, gamma and policy sharing as stated
derieux-model-sizes-setup: Section 3.2, p.6: D = 4, L = 5, arctan; h = 12 for CoinGame and CartPole, h = 100 for MiniGrid
derieux-all-experiments-two-agents: Appendix F.1 p.19 (CoinGame-2 has two agents) and Figure I.4 caption p.29 (MiniGrid, 2 agents); the value claims only these two, matching the passages
derieux-psi-plus-selected: Section 3.3, p.7: 'we select Psi+ as the entanglement scheme to be used in all subsequent experiments'
derieux-cartpole-runs-and-env: Figure 5 caption, p.9 (5 runs of 1,000 epochs) and Appendix F.2, p.20 (independent instances, independent observations)
derieux-coingame-setup: Appendix F.1, p.19: 3 x 3 grid, +1 and -2 rewards, fully observable MDP variant and a POMDP variant without other-agent locations
derieux-minigrid-setup: Appendix F.3, p.21 and Table F.3: 5 x 5 maze, 7 x 7 field of view, POMDP, reward shaping of -1 per step, -2 for standing still and the exploration bonus
derieux-pomdp-classical-reduction: Appendix G.1, p.22: a small classical NN reduces the POMDP observation, and lambda is set to a matrix of ones
derieux-limits: Section 2, p.3 (ideal lossless channel assumed) and Section 4, p.10 (limitation: cost of simulating quantum circuits classically)
derieux-parameters: kept HIGH at the team lead's decision: Section 3.7 and Table 1, p.10: central parameter counts of 1 (eQMARL) and 25 (sCTDE) at h = 12, L = 5 are model-architecture counts the paper states, not a measurement; the value is limited to central parameters on CoinGame-2 as the paper says. The stored LOW treated it as measured; this is a certainty change for the team lead; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
dpqc-feedforward-definition: Section I B 1, p.2, Eqs. (1) and (2): measurement then conditional gate, U0 = I and U1 as given
dpqc-single-qubit-scope: Section I B 1, p.2: the paper states it focuses on single-qubit dynamic operations
dpqc-initialization-ensemble: Section I B 1, p.2: locally scrambling ensemble defined as invariant under conjugation by single-qubit unitaries from a unitary 2-design
dpqc-ancilla-classically-simulated: Section I B 1, p.2: stated as a property of the paper's construction (the control ancilla is unentangled with the circuit)
dpqc-observation-probabilistic-expressiv: Observation 1, Section I B 2, p.3: the argument is complete in the text (F(0) is the identity channel, so all-zero probability parameters give the unitary ansatz); labelled informal but the argument is the whole proof
dpqc-observation-deterministic-realizes-: Observation 2, Section I B 2, p.3: conditions stated (deterministic feedforward on ancillas only) and proved in the text by disconnecting the ancillas with non-entangling gates
dpqc-theorem3a-conditions: Section IV C, p.10: the four conditions of Theorem 3.A; the theorem is proved as Theorem 12 in Appendix C, whose conditions (single operation per parameter, locally scrambling, transfer-matrix form, constant f) match the value
dpqc-bounds-independent-of-n-d: Section IV C, p.11: the bounds (Eqs. 14 and 15, proved as Theorems 12 and 13) contain k, f, phi, alpha and the observable only; no n or d appears
dpqc-theorem12-main-bound: Theorem 12, Appendix C, p.32: stated with its four conditions and proved from Lemmas 5, 10 and 11 in the paper; the value matches Eqs. (C15) and (C16). Lemma 11 treats overlapping paths by assuming conditional independence after a six-case check, which is terse but is in the paper
dpqc-variance-equals-allS-probability: Lemma 5, Appendix B, p.26 to p.27: stated with conditions (locally scrambling, one operation per parameter) and proved in full (Eqs. B16 to B35)
dpqc-feedforward-reset-limits: Lemma 6, Appendix B, p.28 to p.29: the transfer matrix is derived in the proof, and the phi = 0 (dephasing) and phi = pi/2 (reset) limits follow from it as the text shows
dpqc-lemma7-source-of-S: Lemma 7, Appendix C, p.30: lower bound sin^2 phi / 3 independent of other gates and time; proved from the Lemma 6 transfer matrix
dpqc-lemma10-11-path-bounds: Lemmas 10 and 11, Appendix C, p.31 to p.32: both stated and proved in the paper from Lemmas 7 to 9; Lemma 11 uses a six-case check and a conditional-independence argument
dpqc-trainability-definition: Section IV A, p.9: the paper defines trainability (stated as informal, then made precise with epsilon and delta)
dpqc-bp-not-sufficient: Section IV A, p.9 to p.10: the paper states that absence of a barren plateau does not suffice for trainability (with a local-minima example) and that it does not prove trainability of DPQCs
dpqc-parameter-shift: Section IV F, p.12 to p.13, Eqs. (21) to (24): the rule is derived in the text for a rotation exp(-i theta P / 2) and applied to feedforward as a unitary on an ancilla
dpqc-numerics-gradients-autodiff: Section I B 4, p.5: gradients by automatic differentiation executed via classical simulation, for both experiments
dpqc-ground-state-simulator: Section V A, p.14: TensorCircuit tensor network simulator with a purification on 24 qubits
dpqc-ground-state-assumption-gap: Footnote 5, p.13: the paper states its experiments use U3 gates with uniform Euler angles, not an exact single-qubit 2-design, and says what the middle angle should be
dpqc-thermal-bp-theorem-coverage: Section V, p.13: the paper states it does not expect Theorem 3.A to hold for the global infidelity loss and does expect it for the local VarQITE loss; it reports this as an expectation, which the value does
dpqc-thermal-not-scalable-loss: Section I B 4, p.5: the infidelity loss is stated to be not scalable and not covered by the barren-plateau results
dpqc-caveat-small-scale: Section V C, p.16 to p.17, caveat 1: system sizes at most 12 qubits, so an exponentially small gradient might not be very small
dpqc-caveat-no-noise: Section V C, p.17, caveats 2 and 3: no shot noise and no hardware noise in the tensor network simulations
dpqc-caveat-thermal-scalability: Section V C, p.17 to p.18, caveat 4: fidelity loss may need exponential measurement resources; the ODE approach has larger infidelities and no closeness guarantee
dpqc-thermal-open-loss: Section V C, p.18: a suitable scalable loss for thermal state preparation is stated to be an open problem
dpqc-average-case-easy-not-ruled-out: Section I B 5, p.5: the paper states that average-case easiness does not rule out utility and that whether hard instances occur in practice is open
dpqc-feedforward-distance-definition: Section III B, p.8, Definition 4 (informal) and Definition 15 (Appendix A): defined by the paper
dpqc-barren-plateau-definition: Section IV B, p.10: loss function suffers from a barren plateau if for all parameters the gradient variance decays exponentially
dpqc-at-least-as-expressive: Observation 2, Section I B 2, p.3: the narrowed value carries the conditions (deterministic feedforward on ancilla qubits with no loss support) and the text proves it by disconnecting the ancillas
dpqc-no-barren-plateau-condition: Section I B 3 p.4 and Section IV C p.10: the narrowed value carries the conditions; Theorem 12 proves a lower bound on the loss variance, which is the paper's own sense of absence of barren plateaus. The gradient-variance form rests on reference [59] and is graded LOW in dpqc-gradient-variance-implication
dpqc-numerics-size-open: Section VII, p.22: it is stated to be an open task whether the good training behavior persists at larger sizes
dpqc-trainability-open: Section VII, p.22: absence of barren plateaus does not imply trainability, and whether hard instances occur in training is stated as open
ding-task-definition: Section III A, p.3: the task, pulse and weak-measurement sequence and the streaming inputs are stated as the paper's own
ding-simulation-compulsory: Section IV, p.6: stated as a setback of the method; simulation is needed when density matrix elements or fidelity are in the state and reward, since a single shot cannot give the density matrix
ding-simulation-cost-limit: Section IV, p.6: about 7 seconds per episode and a required speedup of about 10^5 (checked on the rendered page: it is a superscript), stated as a limit for real devices
ding-env-setup: Section III B, p.4: action range [0, 3 pi], T = 1 with n = 100 pulses of 0.01, pointer space [-50, 50], 202 x 202 density matrix
ding-agent-and-reward: Sections III B and III C, p.4: ANN with three 64-neuron ReLU layers, reward as negative |rho22 - 1| per step, +1000 above 0.99, penalty 100 if rho11 above 0.05 at the end
ding-training-ppo: Section III C, p.5: PPO, learning rate 1e-3, batch 20, Tensorforce v0.5.3 defaults, action noise standard deviation 0.02
ding-relaxation-terminal-condition: Section III C, p.5: for relaxation on X the terminal condition is population above 0.99 for four neighboring timesteps, stated with its purpose
drl-stream-learning-qubit-control-setup: Abstract p.1 and Section IV p.6: the narrowed value adds that the qubit is simulated by classical computers in the numerical experiments, which the paper states

theory_low.dpqc-theorem1-informal: Theorem 1, Section I B 3, p.3 to p.4 is labelled informal. Its bound has exponent k(f+1) and no phi factor, while the formal Theorem 3.A and Theorem 12 have (sin^2 phi / 3)^k (alpha/5)^(kf) and extra conditions (one operation per parameter, locally scrambling, transfer-matrix form). The quotes drop those conditions. The formal theorem is graded in dpqc-theorem12-main-bound
theory_low.dpqc-theorem1-haar-alpha: Footnote 1, p.4 states alpha = 1 for Haar-random gates; Appendix B Claim 4 says only that the parameters 'can be derived from a calculation analogous to Eq. (A13)' and the Haar transfer matrix (Eq. 19) is taken from reference [26]. Not derived in the paper, so not a definition or a proved result
theory_low.dpqc-theorem2-noise-informal: Theorem 2, p.4 is labelled informal and states the noise as 'after every operation' with infidelity gamma/2, while formal Theorem 13 puts the channel after every two-qubit operation with nonunitarity gamma; its bound drops the phi factor and the conditions. The formal version is graded in dpqc-theorem13-noise-conditions
theory_low.dpqc-observation3-interpolate: Observation 3, p.4 is the authors' summary that the architectures 'interpolate smoothly'; 'smoothly' is not defined or proved, and it rests on the informal Theorem 1
theory_low.dpqc-theorem13-noise-conditions: Theorem 13, Appendix C, p.32 to p.33 is proved in the paper, but the value misstates the replacement: the bound has alpha/5 replaced by (alpha/5)(1 - gamma - delta) + delta, that is alpha replaced by alpha(1 - gamma - delta) + 5 delta, while the value says alpha replaced by alpha(1 - gamma - delta) plus delta. Corrected, this is HIGH on proved result
theory_low.dpqc-sources-and-sinks-intuition: Appendix C, p.31: the 'sources' and 'leaky pipe' passage is the authors' interpretive metaphor after Lemma 10; the rigorous content is Lemma 10 itself, graded separately
theory_low.dpqc-gradient-variance-implication: Section IV F, p.13: the step from loss variance to gradient variance rests on the bound in reference [59, Eq. (C5)], and footnote 4 says the theorems are not stated in this language and the proofs 'can be slightly modified'. A cited result used as a step, and no proof here
theory_low.dpqc-worst-case-hard: Section VI A, p.19 to p.20: an argument, not a proof. It rests on the assumption that universal unitary circuits are hard unless BPP = BQP and on 'easy to satisfy assumptions on the parameterized gates' that are not stated, then on informal Theorem 1
theory_low.dpqc-observation4-average-case-easy: Observation 4, Section VI B, p.20: the argument applies the low-weight Pauli paths algorithm of reference [30] to the purified circuit, so a specific other paper's result is a step; the paper says the case is 'not explicitly considered' there and gives a sketch
